newsitem.title: USA: First Chicago credit card chargeoff rate up.
newsitem.headline: First Chicago credit card chargeoff rate up.

text.p: First Chicago NBD Corp said Monday its credit card chargeoff rate rose to 7.4 percent of managed receivables in the first quarter, up from 6.7 percent in the fourth quarter and 4.8 percent a year ago.

The 30-day delinquency rate for managed credit card receivables was 4.4 percent at the end of the quarter, compared to 4.5 percent at the end of 1996 and 3.6 percent at the end of the first quarter of 1996, the $109.13 billion asset bank holding company said.
Credit card fee revenue was $234 million in the quarter, up from $207 million a year ago.
Overall, First Chicago's provision for credit losses rose to $187 million in the first quarter from $175 million a year ago.

Trading profits in the quarter were $28 million, compared to $36 million a year ago, but up from $12 million in the fourth quarter, First Chicago said. Total market-driven revenues, which include combined trading profits, equity securities gains and investment securities gains, were $107 million, flat from a year ago but up from $83 million in the fourth quarter.

The company said it bought back 7.7 million shares of common stock in the first quarter, bringing the total of repurchases to 15.1 million since October, 1996. First Chicago has repurchase authorizaiton for an additional 24.9 million shares.
Earlier Monday, First Chicago reported net income of $380 million in the quarter, or $1.17 a fully diluted share, compared $340 million, or $1.03 a year ago.
First Chicago shares were down 1/2 at 50-7/8 early Monday.
